relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.evidence: Having received an education at the University of Oslo, he moved to Germany

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.evidence: continued his studies at the University of Heidelberg and the University of Bonn

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.evidence: On his return to Bonn he studied Arabic, and took the degree of Ph.D., his dissertation discussing the Arabic notices of the geography of the Punjab (Commentario geographica historica de Pentapotamia Indica, Bonn, 1827).

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.evidence: Soon after he was admitted Privatdozent

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.role: extraordinary professor of Old Indian language and literature
relations.evidence: in 1830 was appointed extraordinary and in 1840 ordinary professor of Old Indian language and literature. Lassen remained at the University of Bonn to the end of his life.

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.role: ordinary professor of Old Indian language and literature
relations.evidence: in 1840 ordinary professor of Old Indian language and literature. Lassen remained at the University of Bonn to the end of his life.

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.evidence: During this period he published, jointly with Eugène Burnouf, his first work, Essai sur le Pâli (Paris, 1826).

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.evidence: In 1829–1831 Lassen brought out, in conjunction with August Wilhelm von Schlegel, a critical annotated edition of the Hitopadeśa.

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.evidence: Lassen assisted von Schlegel in editing and translating the first two cantos of the epic Rāmāyana (1829-1838).

relations.subject: Christian Lassen
relations.object: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
relations.evidence: and the Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes (7 vols., 1837–1850), started and largely conducted by him
